grammar.title: Ser + Adjetivo - Describing Permanent Characteristics
grammar.content:
The verb SER is used to describe inherent, permanent characteristics of people and things. With appearance, we use 'ser' + adjective.

Conjugation of SER:
Yo soy = I am
Tú eres = You are (informal)
Él/Ella/Usted es = He/She/You(formal) is
Nosotros/as somos = We are
Vosotros/as sois = You(all) are (Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes son = They/You(all) are

Appearance patterns:
Él es alto. = He is tall.
Ella es baja. = She is short.
Ella es rubia. = She is blonde.
Él es moreno. = He is dark-haired.
Ella es guapa. = She is beautiful.
Ellos son jóvenes. = They are young.
Nosotros somos delgados. = We are thin.

Agreement: Adjectives must agree in gender and number with the subject.
Singular: alto/a, bajo/a, rubio/a, moreno/a, guapo/a, delgado/a
Plural: altos/as, bajos/as, rubios/as, morenos/as, guapos/as, delgados/as

Ella es alta y delgada. = She is tall and thin.
Ellos son altos y morenos. = They are tall and dark-haired.
Ellas son bajas y rubias. = They are short and blonde.

Note: 'Ser' is used for permanent characteristics like height, hair color, and general build. For temporary states (tired, sick), use 'estar' instead.
examples:
Mi madre es alta. (My mother is tall.)
Mi padre es bajo. (My father is short.)
Ella es rubia y guapa. (She is blonde and beautiful.)
Él es moreno y delgado. (He is dark-haired and thin.)
Nosotros somos jóvenes. (We are young.)
Ella es vieja. (She is old.)
Tú eres alto. (You are tall.)
Ellos son delgados. (They are thin.)

La chica es guapa y joven. (The girl is pretty and young.)
El hombre es alto y fuerte. (The man is tall and strong.)
Mi hermana es baja y delgada. (My sister is short and thin.)
El niño es pequeño y rubio. (The boy is small and blonde.)
Las mujeres son altas. (The women are tall.)
Los hombres son bajos. (The men are short.)

grammar.title: Estar + Adjetivo - Describing Temporary States and Wearing Clothes
grammar.content:
The verb ESTAR serves two important functions here:

1) Describing temporary physical states:
Estar cansado/a = to be tired
Estar enfermo/a = to be sick
Estar aburrido/a = to be bored
Estar feliz/triste = to be happy/sad

Ella está cansada. = She is tired.
Nosotros estamos felices. = We are happy.
Él está enfermo. = He is sick.

2) Describing what someone is currently WEARING (estar + vestido/a):
Estar = to be
Vestido/a = dressed/wearing clothes

Ella está vestida. = She is dressed.
Él está vestido de negro. = He is dressed in black.
Ellas están vestidas con un vestido rojo. = They are wearing a red dress.

Combined structure for 'to be wearing':
Estar + vestido/a + con + [clothing item]

Él está vestido con una camisa blanca. = He is wearing a white shirt.
Ella está vestida con un vestido negro. = She is wearing a black dress.
Nosotros estamos vestidos con pantalones y camiseta. = We are wearing pants and a t-shirt.
examples:
Ella está cansada hoy. (She is tired today.)
Nosotros estamos contentos. (We are happy.)
Él está enfermo. (He is sick.)
Ellas están aburridas. (They are bored.)
Ella está vestida con una falda roja. (She is wearing a red skirt.)
Él está vestido con un abrigo marrón. (He is wearing a brown coat.)
Nosotros estamos vestidos con ropa deportiva. (We are wearing sportswear.)
¿Cómo estás vestido hoy? (How are you dressed today?)

grammar.title: Tener + Años - Expressing Age
grammar.content:
In Spanish, age is expressed with the verb TENER (to have), not SER (to be). Literally 'to have X years'.

Conjugation of TENER:
Yo tengo = I have
Tú tienes = You have (informal)
Él/Ella/Usted tiene = He/She/You(formal) has
Nosotros/as tenemos = We have
Vosotros/as tenéis = You(all) have (Spain)
Ellos/Ellas/Ustedes tienen = They/You(all) have

Age expressions:
Tengo 25 años. = I am 25 years old.
Ella tiene 30 años. = She is 30 years old.
¿Cuántos años tienes? = How old are you?
Tú tienes 18 años. = You are 18 years old.
Nosotros tenemos 40 años. = We are 40 years old.
¿Cuántos años tiene él? = How old is he?

Asking about age:
¿Cuántos años tienes? (informal)
¿Cuántos años tiene usted? (formal)
¿Cuántos años tiene? (he/she formal)

Age categories:
Niño/a = child
Joven = young person
Adulto/a = adult
Persona mayor = elderly person

Nota: You cannot use 'ser' for age! 'Él es 25 años' is WRONG. Always use 'tener'.
examples:
Tengo 20 años. (I am 20 years old.)
Ella tiene 25 años. (She is 25 years old.)
Tú tienes 30 años. (You are 30 years old.)
¿Cuántos años tienes? - Tengo 18 años. (How old are you? - I am 18 years old.)
Nosotros tenemos 35 años. (We are 35 years old.)
Él tiene 60 años. (He is 60 years old.)
¿Cuántos años tiene ella? - Tiene 45 años. (How old is she? - She is 45 years old.)
Mi madre tiene 50 años. (My mother is 50 years old.)

pronunciation.title: Clothing Vocabulary - Basic Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
Core clothing vocabulary pronunciations:

camisa = kah-MEE-sah (shirt)
camiseta = kah-mee-SEH-tah (t-shirt)
pantalones = pahn-tah-LOH-nes (pants)
vestido = beh-SEE-doh (dress)
falda = FAHL-dah (skirt)
zapatos = sah-PAH-tos (shoes)
chaqueta = chah-KET-ah (jacket)
abrigo = ah-BREE-goh (coat)
suéter = SWEH-ter (sweater)
sandalias = sahn-DAL-ee-ahs (sandals)
botas = BOH-tahs (boots)
zapatillas = zah-pah-TEE-yahs (sneakers)
bufanda = boo-FAHN-dah (scarf)
guantes = GWAHN-tes (gloves)
sombrero = sohm-BREH-roh (hat)
gorra = GOH-rah (cap)
corbata = kor-BAH-tah (tie)
cinturón = seen-too-ROHN (belt)
pantalón = pahn-tah-LOHN (trouser)
calcetín = kal-say-TEEN (sock)
examples:
camisa = kah-MEE-sah
camiseta = kah-mee-SEH-tah
pantalones = pahn-tah-LOH-nes
vestido = beh-SEE-doh
falda = FAHL-dah

abrigo = ah-BREE-goh

exercises.question: What is 'shirt' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'La camisa' = shirt. 'El zapato' = shoe. 'El vestido' = dress. 'La falda' = skirt.

exercises.question: What is 'dress' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'El vestido' = dress. 'El pantalón' = trousers. 'La chaqueta' = jacket. 'La falda' = skirt.

exercises.question: What is 'skirt' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'La falda' = skirt. 'El vestido' = dress. 'La camisa' = shirt. 'Los shorts' = shorts.

exercises.question: What is 'shoes' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Los zapatos' = shoes. 'Las botas' = boots. 'Los calcetines' = socks. 'Las sandalias' = sandals.

exercises.question: What is 'jacket' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'La chaqueta' = jacket. 'El abrigo' = coat. 'El suéter' = sweater. 'La sudadera' = hoodie.

exercises.question: What is 'coat' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'El abrigo' = coat. 'La chaqueta' = jacket. 'El suéter' = sweater. 'La sudadera' = hoodie.

exercises.question: What is 'hat' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'El sombrero' = hat. 'La gorra' = cap. 'La bufanda' = scarf. 'Los guantes' = gloves.

exercises.question: What is 'scarf' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'La bufanda' = scarf. 'Los guantes' = gloves. 'El sombrero' = hat. 'La corbata' = tie.

exercises.question: What is 'gloves' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Los guantes' = gloves. 'La bufanda' = scarf. 'El cinturón' = belt. 'Los pendientes' = earrings.

exercises.question: What is 'tie' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'La corbata' = tie. 'El cinturón' = belt. 'Los guantes' = gloves. 'La bufanda' = scarf.

exercises.question: What is 'belt' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'El cinturón' = belt. 'La corbata' = tie. 'El bolso' = bag. 'Los guantes' = gloves.

exercises.question: What is 'boots' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Las botas' = boots. 'Los zapatos' = shoes. 'Las sandalias' = sandals. 'Las zapatillas' = sneakers.

exercises.question: What is 'socks' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Los calcetines' = socks. 'Las medias' = tights/socks. 'Los zapatos' = shoes. 'Las botas' = boots.

exercises.question: What is 'sweater' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'El suéter' = sweater. 'La chaqueta' = jacket. 'El abrigo' = coat. 'La sudadera' = hoodie.

exercises.question: What is 't-shirt' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'La camiseta' = t-shirt. 'La camisa' = shirt (formal). 'El polo' = polo shirt. 'El suéter' = sweater.

exercises.question: What is 'blonde' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Rubio/a' = blonde. 'Moreno/a' = dark-haired. 'Castaño/a' = brown-haired. 'Pelirrojo/a' = red-haired.

exercises.question: What is 'dark-haired' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Moreno/a' = dark-haired. 'Rubio/a' = blonde. 'Castaño/a' = brown-haired. 'Calvo/a' = bald.

exercises.question: What is 'bald' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Calvo/a' = bald. 'Rubio/a' = blonde. 'Moreno/a' = dark-haired. 'Pelirrojo/a' = red-haired.

exercises.question: What is 'tall' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Alto/a' = tall. 'Bajo/a' = short. 'Grande' = big. 'Pequeño/a' = small.

exercises.question: What is 'short' (height) in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Bajo/a' = short (height). 'Alto/a' = tall. 'Largo/a' = long. 'Corto/a' = short (length).

exercises.question: What is 'thin' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Delgado/a' = thin. 'Fuerte' = strong. 'Gordo/a' = fat. 'Alto/a' = tall.

exercises.question: What is 'black' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Negro/a' = black. 'Rojo/a' = red. 'Azul' = blue. 'Verde' = green.

exercises.question: What is 'blue' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Azul' = blue. 'Rojo/a' = red. 'Verde' = green. 'Negro/a' = black.

exercises.question: What is 'green' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Verde' = green. 'Azul' = blue. 'Amarillo/a' = yellow. 'Rosa' = pink.

exercises.question: What is 'brown' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'Marrón' = brown. 'Gris' = grey. 'Naranja' = orange. 'Rosa' = pink.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ella ___ alta y guapa.' (She is tall and pretty.)
exercises.explanation: Use 'ser' (es) for permanent characteristics like height and beauty. 'Ella es alta y guapa.'

exercises.question: Complete: '___ 25 años.' (I am 25 years old.)
exercises.explanation: In Spanish, age uses 'tener' (to have). 'Tengo 25 años' literally means 'I have 25 years.'

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ella ___ una camisa roja.' (She is wearing a red shirt.)
exercises.explanation: 'Llevar' is used for what someone is wearing. 'Ella lleva una camisa roja.'
